column3: NASB renders “longed for” as “whom I long to see” and adds “my.”
NASB renders “exhort” as “urge” and “to be of the same mind” as “to live in harmony.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Indeed”); “yokefellow” is rendered “comrade,” and “labored together with me in the gospel” is “shared my struggle in the cause of the gospel.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “gentleness” as “forbearing spirit.”
NASB renders “worry about nothing” as “Be anxious for nothing” and adds “let.”
NASB renders “understanding” as “comprehension.”
NASB renders “venerable” as “honorable” and “admirable” as “of good repute,” adds “worthy of,” and renders “think on” as “let your mind dwell on.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “caring” as “concern” and adds “before.”
NASB renders “destitution” as “want” and “in that which I am” as “in whatever circumstances I am.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “to be brought low” as “to get along with humble means” and “to abound” as “to live in prosperity.”
NASB follows the critical text without “Christ”; “I have strength for all things in” is rendered “I can do all things through.”
NASB renders “having fellowship” as “to share with me.”
NASB renders “in the beginning of the gospel” as “at the first preaching of the gospel” and “partnered” as “shared.”
NASB renders “once and twice” as “more than once” and adds “a gift.”
NASB renders “fruit” as “profit” and “abounding” as “increases.”
NASB renders “I have all things” as “I have received everything in full” and “an odor of a sweet smell” as “a fragrant aroma.”
NASB follows the critical text (“riches”); “fill up” is rendered “supply.”
NASB renders “to the ages of the ages” as “forever and ever.”
Close to the Greek.
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text (“your spirit”) without “our,” “Amen,” and the Textus Receptus subscription.
